question: What is the main job of a patient referral form in community health?

options.A: To replace the patient's daily hospital bed ticket
options.B: To serve as a permanent financial receipt for clinic services
options.C: To connect a patient with higher levels of specialized care
options.D: To discharge a patient permanently from all medical follow-up

explanation: You've got this! Referral forms act like a bridge, safely moving a patient from our basic community clinics up to advanced centers when they need extra specialist attention. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T12#GNS225_U2_T12_h1)

question: Why do we always send a written referral form when moving a patient from a primary clinic to a big teaching hospital?

options.A: It ensures continuity of care and prevents miscommunication between facilities
options.B: It legally transfers hospital ownership of the patient's medical history
options.C: It guarantees that the receiving doctor will provide free treatment
options.D: It allows the patient to bypass hospital registration queues entirely

explanation: Great job thinking like a nurse! Writing things down carries the patient's vital clinical details across, so the receiving team instantly knows what care has already been given. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T12#GNS225_U2_T12_h1)

question: What is the main goal of sending a patient on a referral?

options.A: Match the patient's health need with the correct level of care
options.B: Increase the revenue generated by rural health posts
options.C: Reduce the total number of patients visiting government hospitals
options.D: Eliminate the need for community health nurses to write notes

explanation: Spot on! Referrals make sure patients end up right where the right doctors, nurses, and equipment are waiting to handle their specific health condition. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T12#GNS225_U2_T12_h2)

question: How do proper referrals help make the best use of our healthcare system's resources?

options.A: By stopping patients from seeking care at traditional healers
options.B: By reducing the number of nurses needed in rural community posts
options.C: By forcing primary clinics to purchase expensive surgical machinery
options.D: By ensuring tertiary hospitals only treat complex cases requiring specialization

explanation: You're learning fast! When small clinics handle minor issues and send only the tough cases upstairs, expensive big-hospital resources aren't wasted on basic ailments. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T12#GNS225_U2_T12_h2)

question: Which of these is NOT supposed to be on a patient referral form?

options.A: The name of the referring health facility
options.B: The patient's preferred home furniture brand
options.C: The clinical history and present complaints
options.D: The signature and rank of the attending nurse

explanation: Easy one! Referral forms only need medical and personal details required for treatment—furniture choices have nothing to do with patient care. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T12#GNS225_U2_T12_h3)

question: You are filling out a referral form for a pregnant mum with severe pre-eclampsia. What is the most important clinical finding to write down?

options.A: Her personal opinion about hospital food quality
options.B: The distance from her house to the primary healthcare center
options.C: The name of her local community youth organization
options.D: Her most recent blood pressure reading and urine protein test

explanation: Brilliant! Vital signs like her BP and protein levels give the incoming delivery and doctor team immediate, life-saving information. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T12#GNS225_U2_T12_h3)

question: As a community health nurse, what is your very first step when starting a referral?

options.A: Calling an ambulance service before assessing the patient
options.B: Asking the patient to pay administrative referral fees
options.C: Writing a discharge summary for the local health board
options.D: Identifying a clinical condition that exceeds the clinic's capacity

explanation: You've got this. The referral process only begins once you realize the patient's medical needs are too advanced for your local clinic to handle alone. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T12#GNS225_U2_T12_h4)

question: Why should you call or alert the receiving hospital before the patient physically arrives?

options.A: To allow the specialist team time to prepare necessary equipment and space
options.B: To prevent the patient from changing their mind during transit
options.C: To give the nurse permission to leave the clinic early
options.D: To ensure the hospital bed fee is paid in advance by mobile money

explanation: Spot on! Calling ahead gives the emergency or specialist team precious time to ready their staff, drugs, and equipment before the patient rolls in. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T12#GNS225_U2_T12_h4)

question: What is your duty as a nurse regarding a patient's feelings and mindset during a referral?

options.A: Counseling the patient to address fears and explain why care is needed
options.B: Telling the family to ignore advice given by the receiving doctor
options.C: Forcing the patient to leave the clinic immediately without explanation
options.D: Convincing the patient that the local clinic can handle everything

explanation: Wonderful nursing care! Taking time to talk, soothe fears, and explain things helps the patient trust the process and actually go for their treatment. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T12#GNS225_U2_T12_h5)

question: Why is keeping accurate, neat records so vital before you send off a referral?

options.A: It prevents the patient from visiting traditional birth attendants
options.B: It is required to qualify the clinic for international financial grants
options.C: It provides legal protection and proves what interventions were performed
options.D: It allows the nurse to charge extra consultation fees

explanation: You nailed it. Good notes protect you professionally by showing clear evidence of how you assessed, stabilized, and handed over the patient. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T12#GNS225_U2_T12_h5)

question: What exactly is a 'referral feedback loop'?

options.A: A phone call from the ministry of health checking staff attendance
options.B: The routine cleaning schedule of the primary healthcare ambulance
options.C: Information sent back from the receiving hospital to the referring clinic
options.D: A complaint made by a patient about long hospital queues

explanation: You're doing great! The feedback loop simply means the big hospital sends information back to let your clinic know what happened to the patient. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T12#GNS225_U2_T12_h6)

question: How does getting feedback from the hospital help you when you visit patients at home?

options.A: It proves to the village chief that the hospital doctors are competent
options.B: It allows the nurse to charge the patient for specialist consultation
options.C: It gives the nurse a reason to avoid seeing new clinic patients
options.D: It helps the nurse understand the final diagnosis and monitor home recovery

explanation: Spot on! Knowing the hospital's diagnosis and treatment plan lets you provide fantastic, targeted follow-up care right there in the community. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T12#GNS225_U2_T12_h6)

question: Which of these is a very common challenge facing patient referrals in Nigeria?

options.A: An overabundance of working ambulances in every village
options.B: Excessive availability of free medication at tertiary hospitals
options.C: Too many doctors available at primary healthcare centers
options.D: High transportation costs and poor road infrastructure

explanation: You know this context well! Bad roads and expensive transport fares often cause heartbreaking delays for patients trying to reach referral centers. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T12#GNS225_U2_T12_h7)

question: How do money worries directly affect a patient who has been given a referral?

options.A: Patients may refuse or delay going because they cannot afford hospital fees
options.B: Hospitals automatically waive all bills for referred community patients
options.C: The government refunds transport money upon arrival at the gate
options.D: Patients receive double the amount of free drugs to compensate

explanation: So true. Because many people pay out-of-pocket, financial hardship often forces vulnerable patients to stay home instead of getting the specialist care they need. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T12#GNS225_U2_T12_h7)

question: What is the main reason a community clinic keeps a dedicated referral register book?

options.A: To advertise traditional medicine options to local residents
options.B: To calculate the monthly salaries of visiting medical doctors
options.C: To record the personal daily attendance of nursing staff members
options.D: To track outgoing cases, dates, and receiving facilities for auditing

explanation: Brilliant! Logging every referral helps clinics keep a clean record of who was sent out, when, and where they went. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T12#GNS225_U2_T12_h8)

question: Why do nurse managers love doing regular audits of clinic referral records?

options.A: They help identify service gaps, referral trends, and lost patients
options.B: They prove that the clinic requires no further government funding
options.C: They automatically generate transport money for emergency cases
options.D: They ensure that nurses never make mistakes on patient folders

explanation: You've got this! Regular checks show us patterns in patient transfers and highlight where our community care or tracking needs a little boost. [learn more](GNS225_U2_T12#GNS225_U2_T12_h8)
